Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands' Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Jamie Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Today, we'll discuss our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, sales performance and channel strategy, and our outlook for the remainder of the year.

As we wrap up another strong quarter, I'm excited to highlight our key strategic priorities and the progress we've made. Our strategy is centered on delivering sustainable, profitable growth in this challenging CPG landscape, marked by inflation in commodities like cocoa and palm oil, softening demand in mature markets, and shifts toward health, sustainability, and premiumization. We've built this around four pillars: portfolio elevation, innovation and consumer-centricity, sustainability leadership, and operational excellence.

Starting with portfolio elevation, we're optimizing for high-growth, high-margin categories like health and wellness, premium snacks, and plant-based alternatives, while streamlining underperformers. Our Power Brands—Vitality Pure clean-label protein bars, EverFresh plant-based dairy alternatives, and Glow Essentials probiotic skincare—drove 68% of net sales, up from 62% a year ago. They posted 14% organic sales growth, outpacing the total CPG category's 2.1% per NielsenIQ. Vitality Pure gained 220 basis points of market share in U.S. nutrition bars, expanding into 4,500 more Walmart and Kroger doors. We divested our legacy canned soups business for $450 million, unlocking capital for share repurchases and R&D, with portfolio EPS accretion at 8%. We're aiming for Power Brands to fuel 75% of growth by FY2026, lifting gross margins to 48% from 45.2%.

On innovation and consumer-centricity, our R&D spend rose 18% to $280 million, or 2.8% of sales, above the industry average. The Vitality Pure+ adaptogen-infused bars for Gen Z stress relief achieved 25% sell-through in 90 days at Target and Amazon, with 42% repeat rates versus the category's 28%. Our AI-powered Consumer Insights Engine, using Google Cloud and data from 15 million loyalty app users, predicts trends like 30% growth in functional snacks. E-commerce hit 22% of sales, up from 16%, with Amazon velocity up 35%. In Europe, Glow Essentials microbiome shampoos captured 1.5 points in UK natural haircare. Our pipeline includes 12 launches for 2025, like collagen-peptide RTD beverages for the $12 billion market growing at 11% CAGR.

Sustainability leadership is our competitive moat, with 78% of consumers prioritizing eco-friendly brands per our Vitality Pulse survey. We've advanced our 2030 Net Zero roadmap: 72% of products in recyclable packaging, up from 55%, including 100% recycled PET for EverFresh, saving 28,000 tons of plastic and $15 million. Scope 3 emissions fell 12% via RSPO-certified palm oil for 85% of supply. Water use dropped 22% per ton in Brazil. This boosted our MSCI ESG rating to AA, attracted $500 million in green bonds at 75 bps below corporate rates, and lifted brand preference by 6 points for 3% organic growth.

Finally, operational excellence builds resilience. Our Supply Chain Command Center with SAP IBP and Palantir raised forecast accuracy to 92%, cutting inventory 15% to 8.2 weeks and avoiding $40 million stockouts. Productivity savings reached $220 million toward a $1 billion three-year goal via zero-based budgeting and IoT in 45% of plants. Latin America grew 16%, China 4%, EMEA flat core EPS.

These priorities position us for FY2024 organic growth of 6-7%, core EPS up 9-11%, and free cash flow over 95%. I will now turn the call over to Sarah Patel to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Jamie. As Jamie mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $6.2 billion, representing a 7.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 44.5%, driven by pricing actions, productivity gains, and favorable mix, partially offset by commodity inflation. Operating income was $875 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.28. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me unpack our gross margin performance, which expanded 220 basis points year-over-year to 44.5%, the strongest in over two years, with trailing 12-month at 43.9%, up from 42.2%. On a sequential basis, it held steady from Q2's 44.3%. This reflects execution on commodity costs, pricing, and mix across Snacks, Beverages, and Household Essentials.

Commodity costs provided a 110 bps tailwind, with input inflation at 1.2% YoY, down from 8-10% peaks. Cocoa surged 45% to $10,000 per metric ton due to West African harvests, pressuring Chocolate Snacks where it's 15-20% of COGS. Palm oil rose 12% on Indonesian restrictions. Positively, sugar fell 15% to under $0.18 per pound, aiding Beverages, and wheat/corn stabilized. We hedged 75% of 2024 cocoa at $6,800/MT, saving $45 million. Our Supplier Collaboration Portal developed drought-resistant palm with Wilmar, targeting 5% yield gains. Packaging shifts to recycled HDPE saved 50 bps. North America saw 0.8% inflation, EMEA 3.5%, APAC offset by local plantations.

Pricing delivered 180 bps, with 4.1% net pricing on 65% of portfolio. Snacks took 6% hikes on premium NutriBar, elasticity -1.8 versus -2.5 average. Beverages 5.2% on functional drinks. Household at 2.8% with EDLP. North America 55% of tailwind at 4-5%, EMEA 2.9%, APAC 6.5%.

Mix added 70 bps via premiumization: Elevate organic lines at 28% of sales, up from 22%, 52% higher margins. Snacks grew to 45% of sales. U.S. DTC shifted +150 bps premium.

We're targeting 40-50 bps Q4 expansion via $150 million CPG Lean 2.0 savings, AI blending, 80% 2025 hedges, 20 premium SKUs. La Niña risks hedged with $500 million buffer.

Gross margin came in at 44.5% for the quarter—up 120 bps YoY and 50 bps ahead of guidance. Adjusted, it's 45.4%, strongest in three years. Positives: pricing/mix +180 bps with 5.8% realization, premium at 22% of revenue; productivity +100 bps from $85 million CPG Lean 2.0, AI forecasting, 75% cocoa hedges at $3,200/MT. Headwinds: inputs -110 bps (cocoa +45%, dairy +22%), logistics/FX -50 bps. North America 48.3%, EMEA 42.1%, APAC/LatAm 43.7%. Targeting 47-48% by FY2026 via divestitures, blockchain, 15 premium launches. Q3 guide 45.5-46.0%.

Turning to supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings, these delivered $185 million YoY, 210 bps to gross margin, 75 bps to EBITDA. Procurement 45% or $83 million via AI hedging 70% vegetable oils 5% below spot, 12% cocoa/sugar cuts. Manufacturing 30% or $56 million, OEE to 88% with Smart Factory 2.0 robotics, 22% downtime cut in SEA. Logistics 25% or $46 million, 11% freight reduction, OTIF 97.5%, inventory turns 8.2x freeing $320 million. Resilient Supply Chain 2025 targets $750 million, digital twins, 12% Scope 3 drop. Offsetting 60-70% inflation for 200+ bps tailwinds.

On capital expenditures, FY2024 guide $2.4 billion or 4.1% of sales, up 9%, moderating to $2.3 billion FY2025. 45% manufacturing $1.1 billion for Industry 4.0, robotics OEE +15-20%. 25% logistics $600 million, new DCs in Dallas, Rotterdam, Singapore. 20% sustainability $480 million, solar, recycling. North America 50%, EMEA 30%. IRRs over 18%, 110% FCF funded.

Competitive activity has intensified, but our responses are working. In North America, Mondelez/PepsiCo promos gained 1.8 points in snacks; we launched Clean Crunch plant-based, 25% velocity, 2.1 points share, 3.2x ROMI. Coca-Cola Zero +1.4 points; our Hydrate+ NFC cans reclaimed 0.7 points. Europe private labels +2 points; AI forecasting boosted EcoGlow to 92% ACV. EM local cuts; Local Heroes +1.2 points. $250M CPG 2.0 for precision commerce, +2.5 points total share.

A&P spend was $2.8 billion FYTD, 11.2% of sales, up 8%. Q3 $650 million. Advertising 42%, digital 65%; promo 58%. Blended ROMI 3.2x, performance 4.1x. Digital +25% to $900 million, RMNs 28% at 5.5x. AI DCO +18% lift, MTA 85% accuracy. North America 3.5x, APAC 3.8x. 2024 guide $2.9-3.0 billion, 3.0-3.5x ROMI.

Marketing campaign effectiveness improved 12% YoY to 4.8x ROAS, ahead of P&G/Unilever 3.5-4x. Spend $285 million, +8%, 25-point digital shift. Digital 62% sales lift, CAC $18.50, -15%. Refresh Revolution for Refresh Beverages +22% velocity, 6.2x ROAS, AI DCO +41% CTR. Empower Everyday for GlowEssence 5.1x, +17% penetration. NA 5.2x, EMEA 4.1x, APAC 5.5x, LatAm 4.3x. RMNs 22%, clean rooms, ESG +14% premium. FY24 5x+ ROAS.

Next, Lisa will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Sarah. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our Refresh Revolution campaign, which leveraged CTV, social, and in-store for low-sugar sparkling waters, gaining share against Bubly and Aha through rPET bottles and micro-influencers. Empower Everyday drove Gen Z via YouTube Shorts and AR, using app data for personalization. Retail media and sustainability storytelling amplified ROI, supporting premium growth.

Following me, Mike will discuss supply chain performance.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. AI hedging, Smart Factory robotics, and multimodal logistics cut costs and boosted OTIF, while Scope 3 reductions align with consumer preferences. Micro-fulfillment supports e-comm at 28% volume.

After Mike, Elena will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent Vitality Pure+ launch has been well-received, with strong sell-through and repeats from AI insights. Sustainability embeds in innovations like recycled packaging, driving preference and growth.

Finally, Tom will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel at 22%, and we are also investing in our retail partnerships like Walmart and Kroger, countering competitive promos with premium innovations and local plays for share gains.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.

John Smith:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, John. Sustainability is core, with 72% recyclable packaging and 100% rPET for key lines, saving costs and emissions. RSPO palm oil at 85%, water reductions, and ESG campaigns lift preference 6 points and 3% growth, ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Reilly:
Thanks, Maria. APAC and LatAm are priorities, with localized innovations like mango lassis and cassava noodles driving 14% volume in SEA. E-comm via Tmall/JD.com, new DCs in Singapore/Rotterdam for resilience, targeting double-digit growth in plant-based.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley.

David Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Sarah Patel:
Sure, David. Inflation moderated, but we realized 4.1-5.8% pricing with elasticities better than averages, balancing EDLP and premiums. Mix shifts to Elevate lines offset volumes, sustaining velocity amid trade-down slowdown per IRI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Chen with Barclays.

Rachel Chen:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Mike Harlan:
Excellent point, Rachel. AI in hedging locks savings, predictive maintenance cuts downtime 22%, dynamic forecasting to 92% accuracy, digital twins for disruptions. Blue Yonder, Palantir powering OEE to 88%, $185 million savings.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jamie Chen for closing remarks.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
